name: Eversource Energy
headline: A New England power and gas delivery monopoly whose wires cannot be duplicated.
what_short: Regulated New England electric and gas utility
what_it_does: Eversource delivers electricity and gas through regulated utilities in Connecticut, Massachusetts and New Hampshire, including about 1.32 million customers at Connecticut Light & Power. It owns the transmission lines and local wires and earns a regulator-allowed return on them. The cost of the power it supplies is passed through without a profit.
why_it_passed: No competitor can take over its existing transmission and distribution wires, so the franchise stands.
Its earnings are written into regulatory orders, so their shape ten years out can be foreseen.
Allowed returns are stated in the filings, for example 9.5% on 50% equity at its New Hampshire electric utility.
No dishonesty was found in the filings.
why_not_now: A regulator caps what Eversource may earn, so even at a price below the analysis's value range ($71.73 to $81.97 against $67.84), the return is only about 6.45% to 5.52% a year, not the roughly 10% the analysis requires. The 30-year US Treasury bond pays 5.29%, so the extra payment for the risk is thin.
watch: The regulatory climate is the main risk, and a federal ruling on the allowed return on transmission cut earnings.
It recorded an offshore wind liability and has about $28 billion of net debt.
The state denied an earlier sale of its water business, which closed later; management's ability was weighed against.
